advances: A two-fiber product refutes the mixed symmetric-overlap selector at the sharp constant. Its actual global depth meets that constant.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: Reflection about $(z,a)\in S$ sends the other base to $-1$ or $2$, absent from $S$. The only overlap contribution is therefore the area of $K\cap(2a-K)$ from the own fiber, whose unique maximizing $a$ and value are given by pk-w35-reflected-overlap-polygon. At base $0$ use the closed cap $3x-y-100z\ge-669/233$, and at base $1$ use $3x-y+100z\ge100-669/233$. Both caps contain their indicated mark on the boundary. In each case the other base contributes zero, since the maximum of $3x-y$ on $K$ is $8$. The own-fiber trace is exactly the planar cap from the predecessor. Its area divided by $18$ gives the displayed fraction and gap. By the binary-product depth identity of 2acc8bc803acf1c0 with $n=1,d=2$, the normalized mixed maximum equals half the ordinary normalized maximum on $K$. The planar predecessor proves the latter is at least $4/9$.
statement: Let $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(-4,-3),(4,4),(2,3),(-3,0)\}$ and $c=(-182/233,123/233)$. For $S=\{0,1\}\times K$, the mixed-integer set of $[0,1]\times K$, use summed planar area, of total mass $18$. Over $(z,a)\in S$, the mixed overlap mass of $S\cap(2(z,a)-S)$ is maximized exactly at $(0,c)$ and $(1,c)$. Each admits a closed ambient halfspace containing it with normalized mass $70285/325734=2/9-6301/977202$. The global normalized mixed depth maximum is at least $2/9$.
title: Every mixed overlap maximizer can miss the sharp two-fiber bound
